title: COCOMOEstimationInput
description: Schema to guide effort estimation using the COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) technique. Defines input parameters, output table structure, and rules for estimating effort based on KLoC, complexity, and project scale.

estimationTechnique.description: Specifies that COCOMO estimation technique is being used.

projectType.description: Describes the type of project. E.g., Web App, Embedded System, Business Application, AI System

projectScale.description: Defines overall scale of the project influencing effort and number of modules.

timeConstraint.description: Approximate timeline expectation or deadline for the project.

estimatedModules.description: Number of modules (epics) to be generated. Mapped from project scale.

effortRangeHours.description: Minimum and maximum total effort across all modules in hours.

columnDefinitions.description: Defines the structure of each row in the output effort estimation table.

default.description: The logical or functional unit being estimated.
Module complexity: S = Simple, M = Medium, L = Large.
Estimated size of the module in Kilo Lines of Code (thousands of lines of code).
Estimated development effort for the module in person-hours using COCOMO model.
Risk based on complexity, KLoC, and project scale.
Describes the module's nature: UI, Business Logic, Data Access, etc.
Overall effort complexity derived from module type and size.
Effort in person-days, computed from hours as (Effort Estimate ÷ 8).

mappingsAndRules.description: Defines mappings, logic, and rules to calculate effort and classify output attributes.

cocomoEffortFormula.const: Effort = a * (KLoC ^ b), where a and b depend on project class

riskMappingRules: If complexity is 'S' and KLoC < 5 → Risk = Low
If complexity is 'M' and KLoC between 5 and 15 → Risk = Medium
If complexity is 'L' or KLoC > 15 → Risk = High
effortTypeMappingRules: Low if classification is 'Read-Only Module' or KLoC < 5
Medium if classification is 'Business Logic' and KLoC < 15
High if classification is 'UI + Logic' or KLoC > 15

moduleNamePatternRule.const: Use functional names like 'Auth Service', 'Invoice Generator', 'Product Catalog'
